DNS prefix for the AKS cluster
Service principal client ID (appId). If not provided, a managed identity will be used.
Service principal client secret. Required if servicePrincipalClientId is provided.
Name of the Helm chart to install
Version of the Helm chart to install
Base64 encoded docker config JSON for registry credentials

properties.scriptContent:
#!/bin/bash
set -e
 
# Install required tools
for cmd in kubectl helm jq; do
  if ! command -v $cmd &> /dev/null; then
    case $cmd in
      kubectl) az aks install-cli 2>/dev/null || (curl -LO "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -L -s https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl" && chmod +x kubectl && sudo mv kubectl /usr/local/bin/ 2>/dev/null || mv kubectl /usr/local/bin/) ;;
      helm) curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash ;;
      jq) sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y jq 2>/dev/null || (curl -L https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7.1/jq-linux-amd64 -o /tmp/jq && chmod +x /tmp/jq && sudo mv /tmp/jq /usr/local/bin/) ;;
    esac
  fi
done
 
# Setup AKS access
az account set --subscription $SUBSCRIPTION_ID
az aks get-credentials --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --name $CLUSTER_NAME --admin --overwrite-existing
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready nodes --all --timeout=300s || true
 
# Install NGINX Ingress Controller
echo "Installing NGINX Ingress Controller..."
helm repo add ingress-nginx https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx 2>/dev/null || true
helm repo update
helm upgrade --install ingress-nginx ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx \
  --namespace ingress-nginx \
  --create-namespace \
  --set controller.service.externalTrafficPolicy=Local \
  --wait --timeout 300s || true
 
# Wait for Ingress Controller to be ready
echo "Waiting for Ingress Controller to be ready..."
kubectl wait --namespace ingress-nginx \
  --for=condition=ready pod \
  --selector=app.kubernetes.io/component=controller \
  --timeout=300s || true
 
# Install Helm chart
export HELM_EXPERIMENTAL_OCI=1
echo "$HELM_REGISTRY_PASSWORD" | helm registry login -u "$HELM_REGISTRY_USER" --password-stdin "https://$HELM_REGISTRY"
 
cat > /tmp/helm-values.yaml <<EOF
global:
  registryCredentials:
    dockerconfigjson: "$DOCKER_CONFIG_JSON"
ingress:
  enabled: true
  namespace: ingress
  className: nginx
clientGateway:
  service:
    type: ClusterIP
  env:
    ADMIN_USER: "$ADMIN_USER"
    ADMIN_PASSWORD: "$ADMIN_PASSWORD"
frontend:
  service:
    type: ClusterIP
graphDesigner:
  service:
    type: ClusterIP
databaseService:
  env:
    ADMIN_USER: "$ADMIN_USER"
    ADMIN_PASSWORD: "$ADMIN_PASSWORD"
EOF
 
echo "Installing Helm chart..."
helm upgrade --install graphpolaris-services "oci://$HELM_REGISTRY/graphpolaris-helm/$HELM_CHART_NAME" --version "$HELM_CHART_VERSION" -f /tmp/helm-values.yaml
echo "Waiting for deployment to be available..."
kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=600s deployment --all --all-namespaces || true
 
# Wait for Ingress Controller LoadBalancer IP
echo "Waiting for Ingress LoadBalancer IP..."
INGRESS_IP=""
for i in {1..30}; do
  INGRESS_IP=$(kubectl get svc ingress-nginx-controller -n ingress-nginx -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  [ -n "$INGRESS_IP" ] && break
  echo "Waiting for Ingress IP... (attempt $i/30)"
  [ $i -lt 30 ] && sleep 10
done
 
if [ -n "$INGRESS_IP" ]; then
  echo "Ingress IP: $INGRESS_IP"
  export INGRESS_URL="http://$INGRESS_IP"
  export DATABASE_SERVICE_URL="http://database-service.database-service:3000"
 
  # Wait for deployments to be available before updating environment variables
  kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=60s deployment -n graph-designer --all 2>/dev/null || true
  kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=60s deployment -n graph-importer --all 2>/dev/null || true
 
  # Update frontend to use same-origin URLs (relative paths via Ingress)
  # BACKEND_URL uses the Ingress IP so browser can reach it, but it's same-origin now
  kubectl set env deployment/$(kubectl get deployment -n frontend -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -n frontend \
    BACKEND_URL="$INGRESS_URL" \
    BACKEND_AUTH="$INGRESS_URL/api/auth" \
    BACKEND_WSS_URL="ws://$INGRESS_IP/ws" 2>/dev/null || true
 
  # Update graph-designer with same-origin URLs
  kubectl set env deployment/$(kubectl get deployment -n graph-designer -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -n graph-designer \
    BACKEND_URL="$INGRESS_URL" \
    BACKEND_AUTH="$INGRESS_URL/api/auth" \
    BACKEND_WSS_URL="ws://$INGRESS_IP/ws" 2>/dev/null || true
 
  # Update graph-importer - uses internal service URL
  kubectl set env deployment/$(kubectl get deployment -n graph-importer -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -n graph-importer \
    SAVE_STATE_SERVICE_URL="http://client-gateway.client-gateway:3001" 2>/dev/null || true
 
  # Update client-gateway with ALLOWED_ORIGINS (same as Ingress URL)
  kubectl set env deployment/$(kubectl get deployment -n client-gateway -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -n client-gateway \
    ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$INGRESS_URL" \
    BETTER_AUTH_URL="$INGRESS_URL" \
    BETTER_AUTH_SECRET="6xAURODghVb43l79r4omr6rrWrunDkSC" 2>/dev/null || true
else
  echo "Warning: Could not get Ingress IP, services may not be accessible externally"
fi
 
# Run database migrations
if kubectl get namespace client-gateway &>/dev/null; then
  kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=client-gateway -n client-gateway --timeout=120s || true
  CLIENT_GATEWAY_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n client-gateway -l app.kubernetes.io/name=client-gateway -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 
  if [ -n "$CLIENT_GATEWAY_POD" ]; then
    # Check postgres readiness
    for ns in client-gateway postgres-common; do
      if kubectl get postgresql postgres-common -n $ns &>/dev/null; then
        kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l application=spilo -n $ns --timeout=300s 2>/dev/null && break
      fi
    done
 
    # Wait for postgres password to be synced (operator creates secret before setting password in DB)
    echo "Waiting for PostgreSQL password to be synced..."
    PG_PASSWORD_SYNCED=false
    for i in {1..30}; do
      PG_PASSWORD=$(kubectl get secret -n client-gateway publicgp.postgres-common.credentials.postgresql.acid.zalan.do -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' 2>/dev/null | base64 -d)
      if [ -n "$PG_PASSWORD" ]; then
        if kubectl exec -n client-gateway postgres-common-0 -- psql "postgresql://publicgp:${PG_PASSWORD}@localhost:5432/publicgp" -c "SELECT 1" &>/dev/null; then
          echo "PostgreSQL password synced successfully!"
          PG_PASSWORD_SYNCED=true
          break
        fi
      fi
      echo "Waiting for password sync... (attempt $i/30)"
      sleep 10
    done
 
    # Restart client-gateway pods to ensure they connect with the correct password
    if [ "$PG_PASSWORD_SYNCED" = true ]; then
      echo "Restarting client-gateway pods to reconnect with synced password..."
      kubectl rollout restart deployment -n client-gateway -l app.kubernetes.io/name=client-gateway 2>/dev/null || true
      kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=client-gateway -n client-gateway --timeout=120s || true
      CLIENT_GATEWAY_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n client-gateway -l app.kubernetes.io/name=client-gateway -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    fi
 
    # Verify database environment variables are set correctly
    echo "=== Verifying database environment variables in pod: $CLIENT_GATEWAY_POD ==="
    kubectl exec -n client-gateway $CLIENT_GATEWAY_POD -- sh -c '
      echo "POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-<not set>}"
      if [ -n "$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" ]; then
        echo "POSTGRES_PASSWORD: <set (hidden)>"
      else
        echo "POSTGRES_PASSWORD: <not set>"
      fi
      echo "POSTGRES_HOST: ${POSTGRES_HOST:-<not set>}"
      echo "POSTGRES_PORT: ${POSTGRES_PORT:-<not set>}"
      echo "POSTGRES_NAME: ${POSTGRES_NAME:-<not set>}"
      echo "DATABASE_SSL: ${DATABASE_SSL:-<not set>}"
    '
    echo "=== End of environment variable check ==="
   
    # Run migration
    # Since it works when you exec into the pod manually, the password is correct
    # The difference might be the execution context. Let's match your manual exec exactly:
    # - Same working directory (/app)
    # - Same user context (container runs as 'bun' user)
    # - Same command: bun db:migrate
    echo "=== Running migration in pod: $CLIENT_GATEWAY_POD ==="
    echo "Note: Verify this is the same pod you use when exec'ing manually"
   
    # Wait 180 seconds to ensure pod is fully ready and environment is properly initialized
    echo "Waiting 180 seconds before running migration..."
    sleep 180
    CLIENT_GATEWAY_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n client-gateway -l app.kubernetes.io/name=client-gateway -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
   
    # Run the migration with retry logic
    # Retry up to 10 times with 15 second delays between attempts
    MAX_RETRIES=10
    RETRY_DELAY=15
    RETRY_COUNT=0
    MIGRATION_SUCCESS=false
   
    while [ $RETRY_COUNT -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; do
      if [ $RETRY_COUNT -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "Migration attempt $RETRY_COUNT failed. Retrying in $RETRY_DELAY seconds... (attempt $((RETRY_COUNT + 1))/$MAX_RETRIES)"
        sleep $RETRY_DELAY
        # Refresh pod name in case it changed
        CLIENT_GATEWAY_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n client-gateway -l app.kubernetes.io/name=client-gateway -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      else
        echo "Running migration (attempt $((RETRY_COUNT + 1))/$MAX_RETRIES)..."
      fi
     
      # Run the migration - the container runs as 'bun' user by default
      # Ensure we're in /app and run the exact same command
      if kubectl exec -n client-gateway $CLIENT_GATEWAY_POD -- sh -c "cd /app && bun db:migrate"; then
        echo "Migration completed successfully!"
        MIGRATION_SUCCESS=true
        break
      else
        RETRY_COUNT=$((RETRY_COUNT + 1))
      fi
    done
   
    if [ "$MIGRATION_SUCCESS" = false ]; then
      echo "ERROR: Migration failed after $MAX_RETRIES attempts"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
fi
 
# Collect service access information
echo "Collecting service access information..."
 
# Get Ingress IP for output
INGRESS_IP=$(kubectl get svc ingress-nginx-controller -n ingress-nginx -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null || echo "Pending")
 
# Build JSON output with Ingress URL as the main access point
OUTPUT_JSON=$(cat <<EOF
{
  "ingress_url": "http://$INGRESS_IP",
  "services": {
    "frontend": "http://$INGRESS_IP/",
    "api": "http://$INGRESS_IP/api",
    "websocket": "ws://$INGRESS_IP/ws",
    "designer": "http://$INGRESS_IP/designer"
  }
}
EOF
)
 
# Validate JSON output
if ! echo "$OUTPUT_JSON" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Warning: Failed to generate valid JSON, creating empty result"
  OUTPUT_JSON='{"ingress_url":"","services":{}}'
fi
 
# Save to temp file for display
echo "$OUTPUT_JSON" > /tmp/services-output.json
 
# Output to deployment script output path (Azure expects this to be valid JSON)
# Azure will make this available as .outputs.result, which the template then parses
# Ensure it's written as a single line without trailing newlines
if [ -n "${AZ_SCRIPTS_OUTPUT_PATH:-}" ]; then
  COMPACT_JSON=$(echo "$OUTPUT_JSON" | jq -c '.')
  printf '%s' "$COMPACT_JSON" > "$AZ_SCRIPTS_OUTPUT_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true
  echo "Output written to $AZ_SCRIPTS_OUTPUT_PATH: $(cat "$AZ_SCRIPTS_OUTPUT_PATH" 2>/dev/null | head -c 200)"
fi
 
echo -e "\n=== GraphPolaris Access URLs ==="
echo "Main URL: http://$INGRESS_IP"
echo "API: http://$INGRESS_IP/api"
echo "WebSocket: ws://$INGRESS_IP/ws"
echo "Designer: http://$INGRESS_IP/designer"
